meaning: “Unless A happens first, B can't happen.” The second half is usually negative.
connection: Verb nai-form／い-adj. くない／noun・な-adj. でない + ことには

senses.label: Unless ... first, can't ...
senses.meaning: A is a necessary condition for B. Without A, B is out of the question. The second half must be negative. It stresses a “prerequisite” more strongly than 「〜なければ」.
senses.connection: Verb nai-form + ことには + 〜ない／分からない／始まらない／何とも言えない
examples: I won't know if it's any good until I actually try it.
Unless the president gives approval, we can't move the plan forward.
I can't say anything until I meet the person myself.

senses.label: With adjectives and nouns
senses.meaning: With adjectives or nouns, it means “unless something is in a certain state, it won't work”. い-adjectives take 「〜くないことには」. Nouns and な-adjectives take 「〜でないことには」.
senses.connection: い-adj. くない／noun・な-adj. でない + ことには
examples: Unless you're physically strong, you can't keep doing this job.
Unless the price comes down a bit, it probably won't sell well.

notes: The second half must be negative. It can't be followed by a positive intention or request. ✕「勉強しないことには、遊びに行こう」.
Often paired with 「とにかく」 or 「まず」. Men sometimes shorten it to 「〜ないことにゃ」 in casual speech.
Don't confuse it with 「〜ないことはない」 (it's not that ... not). They differ by one character but mean something completely different.

daily.title: Unsure about clothes online
daily.description: A friend recommends some clothes, and you say you need to try them on first.
daily.example: I can't tell if the size fits until I try it on.

daily.title: Planning what to pack
daily.description: You talk with family about what to bring and say you need the forecast first.
daily.example: I can't decide what to take until I check the weather forecast.

daily.title: Learning a language
daily.description: You share your experience of learning to speak a language.
daily.example: Unless you speak every day, your conversation skills won't improve.

work.title: Holding off in a meeting
work.description: The person in charge says they can't judge without full data.
work.example: We can't make a decision until we have detailed data.

work.title: Replying to a client
work.description: You say you must first check the other company's intentions.
work.example: We are unable to reply until we confirm your company's intentions.

etymology: Negative 「ない」 + the formal noun 「こと」 + 「には」 (marking a situation). Literally “in the situation of not doing ...”. It became fixed as “unless ... first”.

similar.title: 〜なければ
similar.explanation: 「〜なければ」 is a general negative condition. Anything can follow. 「〜ないことには」 stresses a prerequisite, is followed only by negative results, and sounds stronger.

similar.title: 〜てからでないと
similar.explanation: Also means “can't ... until ...”, but focuses on time order (do A, then B). 「〜ないことには」 focuses on whether the condition itself is met.

similar.title: 〜ないことはない
similar.explanation: A double negative: “it's not that ... not”, “it's not impossible”. Looks similar to 「〜ないことには」 but means something very different.

similar.title: 〜なくして（は）
similar.explanation: N1, written style, used after nouns (「努力なくしては」): “without ..., can't ...”. 「〜ないことには」 mainly follows verbs and is common in speech too.

meaning: A strong wish for something hard to achieve: “Isn't there some way to ...?”, “If only ...”.
connection: Verb nai-form (usually potential) + ものか／ものだろうか／ものでしょうか

senses.label: Strong wish
senses.meaning: It looks like a question, but it expresses a strong wish for something difficult: “Is there any way to ...?” Often used with 「何とか」, 「どうにか」, or 「もう少し」. Mostly said to oneself or thought privately.
senses.connection: Potential verb nai-form／ならない + ものか (+ と思う・と考える)
examples: Isn't there some way I can help him?
Can't something be done about this traffic jam?
I'm wondering if there's a way to travel a little more cheaply.

senses.label: Polite inquiry
senses.meaning: 「〜ないものだろうか」 and 「〜ないものでしょうか」 sound softer. They are used to politely express a hope and ask whether it might be possible.
senses.connection: Verb nai-form + ものだろうか／ものでしょうか (often with 「〜てもらえない」 or 「〜ていただけない」)
examples: Would it be possible to extend the deadline by one more day?
Isn't there anyone who can solve this problem?

notes: It is 「ない」 + 「か」, but it's not a negative question. It expresses “I wish I could ...”.
The verb before it is usually potential (「〜られない」, 「〜できない」), or 「ならない」, 「もらえない」, etc.
Different from 「〜ものか」 (“No way!”, “I'll never ...”). 「ものか」 follows the affirmative and expresses strong denial. 「ないものか」 follows the negative and expresses a wish.
The tone is rather written and formal. In speech, 「〜ないかな」 is more common.

daily.title: Trouble sleeping
daily.description: Someone who can't sleep well mutters to themselves.
daily.example: If only I could sleep soundly every night.

daily.title: Wanting a pet
daily.description: A child living in an apartment grumbles to the family.
daily.example: I wish we could have a cat at our place too.

daily.title: Reading an opinion column
daily.description: An editorial or essay expresses the writer's wish.
daily.example: Isn't there some way to put an end to conflict?

work.title: Asking the boss for budget
work.description: A staff member politely asks the boss for more budget.
work.example: Would it be possible to increase the budget a little more?

work.title: Improving operations
work.description: In a meeting, you explain why you're considering a new system.
work.example: We're looking at a new system, hoping to find a way to work more efficiently.

etymology: Negative 「ない」 + the formal noun 「もの」 + the question particle 「か」. 「ものか」 originally expressed a strong or rhetorical question. After a negative, the rhetorical “Can't it be ...?” gradually turned into a wish: “If only ...”.

similar.title: 〜ないかな (wish)
similar.explanation: Casual. A light wish: “I hope ...”, “I wish ...” (「早く来ないかな」). 「〜ないものか」 is stronger, more formal, and usually about something hard to achieve.

similar.title: 〜ものか・〜もんか
similar.explanation: Follows the affirmative and expresses strong denial: “No way!”, “I'll never ...” (「負けるものか」). Almost the opposite of 「ないものか」.

similar.title: 〜たいものだ
similar.explanation: Also expresses a strong wish, but as a statement. 「〜ないものか」 is a question, with a sense of searching for a way.

meaning: “On the occasion of ...”: at the start of (or while preparing for) something important. Formal and written.
connection: Noun／verb dictionary form + にあたって・にあたり・にあたっての + noun

senses.label: On the occasion of
senses.meaning: Used when starting something important or special. Common in speeches, notices, and documents. 「にあたり」 is more written than 「にあたって」.
senses.connection: Noun (開始・出発・就任・入学, etc.)／verb dictionary form + にあたって／にあたり、／にあたっての + noun
examples: As the new year began, I set my goals for the year.
To open this meeting, allow me to say a few words.
We've put together some points to note when studying abroad.

senses.label: When undertaking ...
senses.meaning: Shows what you need to keep in mind or prepare when taking on a task. The second half is usually “must ...”, “should ...”, or “please ...”.
senses.connection: Noun／verb dictionary form + にあたっては
examples: When renting an apartment, you need to read the contract carefully.
When conducting the survey, please take great care with personal information.

notes: Used for special or important occasions, not everyday trivia. ✕「ご飯を食べるにあたって」.
「にあたり」 is the continuative form and more written. Formal speeches often use 「にあたりまして」.
Written in kanji as 「に当たって」. Don't confuse it with the literal meaning “hit”, as in 「ボールが頭に当たって」.

daily.title: Reading an admission guide
daily.description: You see it in the school's admission handbook.
daily.example: Please prepare the required documents for admission.

daily.title: Visiting before marriage
daily.description: You tell a friend how you prepared for your wedding.
daily.example: Before getting married, we went to greet our parents.

work.title: Opening a new shop
work.description: The owner thanks guests at the opening ceremony.
work.example: On the occasion of today's opening, I offer my heartfelt thanks.

work.title: Internal notice
work.description: A notice from General Affairs to all staff.
work.example: We will hold a briefing on the introduction of the new system.

work.title: Inaugural speech
work.description: The new president speaks at an all-staff meeting.
work.example: On taking office as president, allow me to share my aspirations.

etymology: 「あたる（当たる）」 originally means “to hit, to face directly”. It extended to “to face (a moment)”. 「〜にあたって」 means “right at this moment of ...”, so it became a written way to say “on the occasion of”.

similar.title: 〜に際して
similar.explanation: Almost the same meaning, both written. 「に際して」 is more objective: “at that time”. 「にあたって」 stresses actively preparing for something important that's about to start.

similar.title: 〜際（に）
similar.explanation: Just means “when ...” and works for ordinary matters (「お降りの際は」). 「にあたって」 is limited to important or special events.

similar.title: 〜に先立って
similar.explanation: Clearly means “before ... (do something first)”. 「にあたって」 covers both before and during, focusing on “this moment”.

meaning: B changes or adjusts according to differences or changes in A.
connection: Noun + に応じて・に応じ・に応じた + noun

senses.label: According to
senses.meaning: B changes to match A. A is usually a noun that varies or changes: 「能力」, 「年齢」, 「状況」, 「希望」, 「収入」.
senses.connection: Noun + に応じて／に応じ、
examples: The amount of tax changes according to income.
We change the menu according to the season.
Keep doing exercise that suits your stamina, without overdoing it.

senses.label: Matching ...
senses.meaning: 「に応じた + noun」 modifies a noun: “suited to ...”, “in proportion to ...”.
senses.connection: Noun + に応じた + noun
examples: We pay a salary based on experience.
Teaching tailored to each person's level is important.

senses.label: Respond to / accept
senses.meaning: As a verb, 「〜に応じる」 means to accept or respond to a request, invitation, interview, etc.
senses.connection: Noun (要求・依頼・注文・取材・誘い, etc.) + に応じる／に応じて
examples: The company agreed to the union's demands.
He agreed to the reporter's interview and talked about the incident.

notes: A must be something with several possibilities that can vary, and B changes with it.
「応じる」 is read 「おうじる」; 「応える」 is read 「こたえる」. You say 「期待に応える」, not 「期待に応じる」.
Common in writing and business. In speech, 「〜によって」 and 「〜に合わせて」 are also common.

daily.title: At the gym
daily.description: A trainer explains the program to a new member.
daily.example: Let's plan your workout based on your age and fitness.

daily.title: Ordering a set meal
daily.description: A server tells a customer the rice portion can be adjusted.
daily.example: You can adjust the amount of rice to your liking.

daily.title: Reading a job ad
daily.description: You read it while browsing part-time job listings.
daily.example: The hourly wage depends on experience.

work.title: Proposal to a client
work.description: A salesperson presents options to a client.
work.example: We'll propose a plan that fits your budget.

work.title: Explaining HR policy
work.description: HR explains the bonus system.
work.example: Bonuses are paid according to performance.

etymology: 「応じる」 is a サ-irregular verb made of the kanji 「応」 + 「じる（ずる）」. It originally means “to respond, to answer”. From “responding to someone” it extended to “changing in line with ...”.

similar.title: 〜によって
similar.explanation: Can also mean “differs depending on ...” (「人によって違う」), focusing on objective differences. 「に応じて」 focuses on actively adjusting to match.

similar.title: 〜に合わせて
similar.explanation: Focuses on “matching, fitting in with ...” (「音楽に合わせて踊る」). 「に応じて」 focuses on varying with degree or circumstances.

similar.title: 〜次第で
similar.explanation: Stresses “it all depends on ...”; A decides the result. 「に応じて」 focuses on changing proportionally or case by case.

similar.title: 〜にこたえて
similar.explanation: 「応える」 means “to respond to and meet expectations or requests”. 「応じる」 means “to go by, to accept”.

meaning: Affects or concerns something serious (life, reputation, etc.), or is involved in something.
connection: Noun + にかかわる／にかかわって／にかかわった

senses.label: Affects (seriously)
senses.meaning: Has a major impact on something important. A is usually 「命」, 「名誉」, 「信用」, 「将来」, 「健康」, etc. The tone is serious; 「命にかかわる」 (life-threatening) is very common.
senses.connection: Noun + にかかわる (+ 問題・病気, etc.)
examples: This is a serious, life-or-death problem.
A mistake like that would damage the company's credibility.

senses.label: Be involved in
senses.meaning: Being part of some work or connected to something. A neutral “related to, involved in”.
senses.connection: Noun + にかかわる／にかかわって／にかかわった + noun
examples: I've worked in education for many years.
A person involved in the incident was arrested.
He's involved in making the movie.

notes: Written in kanji as 「関わる」 or 「係わる」, and often in kana.
「〜にかかわらず」 (regardless of) and 「〜にもかかわらず」 (despite) are different grammar points. Don't mix them up.
Sense 1 is mostly about bad effects (threatening ...). Sense 2 is a neutral “related to, involved in”.

daily.title: Urging a family member to see a doctor
daily.description: Family persuade someone who doesn't want to go to the hospital.
daily.example: If you leave that illness alone, it could be life-threatening.

daily.title: Talking about future dreams
daily.description: A student talks with a friend about the job they want.
daily.example: In the future, I want a job working with children.

daily.title: Reading the news
daily.description: You see a report about a personal data leak.
daily.example: Information related to privacy was leaked.

work.title: Quality meeting
work.description: The boss asks for a quality issue to be handled right away.
work.example: This issue affects quality, so please deal with it immediately.

work.title: Job interview
work.description: A candidate describes their past work.
work.example: Since joining the company, I've been involved in developing new products.

etymology: 「かかわる」 was 「かかはる」 in old Japanese, meaning “to be tied to, to be caught up in”. The kanji 「関」 and 「係」 were borrowed for “connection”. From “being connected”, it came to mean “having a serious impact on ...”.

similar.title: 〜に関して
similar.explanation: Only marks a topic: “about ...” (「環境に関して話す」). 「にかかわる」 shows a real connection, impact, or involvement, and sounds weightier.

similar.title: 〜にかかわらず
similar.explanation: Means “regardless of ...”, the opposite idea of 「にかかわる」.

similar.title: 〜にかかっている
similar.explanation: Means “depends on ...”; A is the deciding factor. With 「にかかわる」, A is the important thing being affected.

meaning: The success or outcome depends entirely on A: “it all comes down to ...”.
connection: Noun／〜かどうか／question word ... か + にかかっている

senses.label: Depends on
senses.meaning: The result is decided entirely by A. Common pattern: 「AはBにかかっている」. The subject is often 「成功」, 「結果」, 「将来」, 「勝敗」. A is often 「努力」, 「やる気」, or a 「〜かどうか」 clause.
senses.connection: Noun／〜かどうか／question word ... か + にかかっている／にかかっています
examples: Whether we win the game depends on the players' efforts.
This company's future depends on whether the new product sells.
In the end, it all comes down to the person's own motivation.

senses.label: Rests on someone's shoulders
senses.meaning: 「〜の肩にかかっている」 or 「〜の双肩にかかっている」 means a heavy responsibility rests on someone; everything depends on them.
senses.connection: Person + の肩／の双肩 + にかかっている
examples: The team's fate rests on the captain's shoulders.
The whole family's livelihood rests on his shoulders.

notes: 「かかる」 originally means “to hang”. 「壁に絵がかかっている」 (a picture hangs on the wall) is not this grammar.
「医者にかかっている」 (seeing a doctor) is not this grammar either.
Close in meaning to 「〜次第だ」. 「次第」 is more common in speech.

daily.title: Encouraging a child before exams
daily.description: A parent talks to a child preparing for exams.
daily.example: Whether you pass or not depends on how hard you work.

daily.title: Planning a weekend barbecue
daily.description: Friends are worried about the weather.
daily.example: Whether we can have the barbecue tomorrow depends on the weather.

daily.title: Reading sports news
daily.description: You see it in a report about the finals.
daily.example: The championship depends on the result of the final match.

work.title: Project kickoff
work.description: A project manager speaks to the team.
work.example: The success of this project depends on everyone's cooperation.

work.title: Management meeting
work.description: The president analyzes this term's results.
work.example: This term's results depend on whether the new product becomes a hit.

etymology: 「かかる（掛かる）」 originally means “to hang, to be hung on ...”. From the image of something hanging on one support point, it came to mean “to rest entirely on ...”, “to depend on ...”.

similar.title: 〜次第だ・〜次第で
similar.explanation: Similar meaning. 「次第」 attaches directly to nouns and is more casual (「やる気次第だ」). 「にかかっている」 carries the image of a heavy weight hanging on something and sounds more serious.

similar.title: 〜によって
similar.explanation: Means “differs depending on ...”, focusing on differences. 「にかかっている」 focuses on the result being fully controlled by A.

similar.title: 〜にかかわる
similar.explanation: Means “affects, concerns”; A is the important thing affected (「命にかかわる」). With 「にかかっている」, A is the deciding factor.

similar.title: 〜にかかったら
similar.explanation: N1: “in the hands of ...” (「彼にかかったら、どんな機械もすぐ直る」). Different from this grammar.

meaning: “When it comes to ... (no one can beat them)”. Used to praise someone's skill in a field or to express confidence.
connection: Noun + にかけては／にかけても

senses.label: Best at ...
senses.meaning: Someone is the best in a field or skill; no one can match them. The second half is usually positive: 「誰にも負けない」, 「右に出る者はいない」, 「自信がある」, 「一番だ」.
senses.connection: Noun (skill・field) + にかけては
examples: When it comes to cooking, no one can beat my mom.
When it comes to running fast, he's the best in the class.
When it comes to math, I'm confident I can beat anyone.

senses.label: Also good at ...
senses.meaning: 「にかけても」 means “also (just as good) when it comes to ...”. Used to add another strength on top of one already mentioned.
senses.connection: Noun + にかけても
examples: He's a great singer, and he dances at a professional level too.

notes: Used to evaluate skill or ability; the second half is positive. ✕「遅刻にかけては」 (unless joking).
In 「夜から朝にかけては雨」, 「にかけて」 marks a range of time or place, followed by 「は」. That's not this grammar.
In casual speech, you can say 「〜にかけちゃ」.

daily.title: Talking about siblings
daily.description: You mention your younger brother's gaming skills.
daily.example: When it comes to video games, I'm no match for my little brother.

daily.title: Introducing your strengths
daily.description: You introduce yourself to the class at the start of term.
daily.example: When it comes to getting up early, I'm confident.

daily.title: Reading sports news
daily.description: A report praises an athlete.
daily.example: When it comes to speed, no player can top him.

work.title: Recommending staff
work.description: A department head recommends a team member to a director.
work.example: When it comes to negotiation skills, she's the best in the company.

work.title: Company pitch
work.description: Presenting your company's strengths to a client.
work.example: When it comes to quality, we're confident we can beat any other company.

etymology: 「かける（掛ける）」 can mean “to stake, to bet” (as in 「命をかける」). One theory: 「〜にかけては」 came from “staking everything on this point” and became “as far as ... goes (the best)”.

similar.title: 〜において
similar.explanation: Written; neutrally marks a setting or field: “in ...”. 「にかけては」 carries a judgment: “the best, the most skilled”.

similar.title: 〜から〜にかけて
similar.explanation: Marks a range of time or space: “from ... to ..., around ...”. Same form as 「にかけては」, different meaning.

similar.title: 〜に関して
similar.explanation: Neutral “about ...”. 「にかけては」 is only for praising outstanding ability.

meaning: Adds B on top of A: “in addition to ...”, “not only ... but also ...”.
connection: Noun + に加えて・に加え

senses.label: In addition to
senses.meaning: Adds another thing of the same kind on top of something. Mostly used in writing, news, and formal settings. The second half often has 「〜も」.
senses.connection: Noun + に加えて／に加え、
examples: On top of the rain, the wind is getting stronger.
This job requires Chinese in addition to English.
On top of rising prices, even our salaries went down.

senses.label: With verbs and clauses
senses.meaning: With verbs or adjectives, first turn them into nouns with 「こと」 or 「の」, then add 「に加えて」.
senses.connection: Verb・adjective plain form + こと／の + に加えて
examples: Not only is he good at his job, he's also a nice person.
It's far from the station, and on top of that the rent is high.

notes: Fairly written in tone. In speech, 「〜だけでなく」 and 「それに」 are common.
A and B are usually of the same kind and direction (both good or both bad).
It can also be used as a conjunction at the start of a sentence, 「加えて、」: “in addition, moreover”.
Don't confuse it with the literal verb 「加える」 (to add), as in 「スープに塩を加える」.

daily.title: Complaining about the rainy season
daily.description: Complaining about the weather with a friend in summer.
daily.example: It's not just hot, it's terribly humid too.

daily.title: Watching the weather forecast
daily.description: A TV forecast gives a warning.
daily.example: Along with heavy rain, watch out for lightning too.

daily.title: Recommending a restaurant
daily.description: Recommending your favorite place to a friend.
daily.example: This place has great food, and the service is good too.

work.title: Job posting
work.description: Requirements in a company's job ad.
work.example: We're looking for people with English skills in addition to work experience.

work.title: Explaining a price increase
work.description: Explaining the reasons for raising prices to a client.
work.example: In addition to labor costs, raw material costs are also rising.

etymology: 「加える（くわえる）」 means “to add”. 「〜に加えて」 literally means “adding on top of ...”, so it became a written expression for adding things up.

similar.title: 〜上（に）
similar.explanation: Also adds things up, attaching directly to plain-form verbs and adjectives (「安い上においしい」). 「に加えて」 mainly follows nouns and is written and objective.

similar.title: 〜だけでなく
similar.explanation: Common in both speech and writing; follows any word type. 「に加えて」 is more written, often seen in news and documents.

similar.title: 〜のみならず
similar.explanation: Even more written and stiff: “not only ... but also ...”. 「に加えて」 focuses on “adding on top”.

meaning: Responding to someone's expectations or requests, and working to meet them.
connection: Noun + にこたえて・にこたえ・にこたえる + noun (kanji: 「応えて」)

senses.label: Respond to / live up to
senses.meaning: Acting in response to someone's expectations, requests, or wishes, and making them happen. A is usually 「期待」, 「要望」, 「声援」, 「ニーズ」, 「リクエスト」, etc.
senses.connection: Noun + にこたえて／にこたえ、
examples: Responding to the fans' cheers, the player waved.
Living up to my parents' expectations, I became a doctor.
In response to customer requests, we extended our business hours.

senses.label: That meets ...
senses.meaning: 「にこたえる + noun」 modifies a noun: “that meets ...”. The negative potential 「期待にこたえられない」 is also common.
senses.connection: Noun + にこたえる／にこたえた + noun; noun + にこたえられる／にこたえられない
examples: We develop products that meet consumer needs.
I'm sorry I couldn't live up to everyone's expectations.

notes: The kanji is 「応える」, read 「こたえる」. 「質問に答える」 (answer a question) is not this grammar.
A is the other person's expectation or request. This differs from 「に応じて」, which means “according to”.
Mostly about actively meeting others' wishes. Common in news, ads, and thank-you speeches.

daily.title: At a concert
daily.description: Chatting with a friend about the encore.
daily.example: In response to the encore, they sang one more song for us.

daily.title: A child studying for exams
daily.description: Talking about why a child studies so hard.
daily.example: They study every day, trying to live up to their parents' expectations.

daily.title: Reading sports news
daily.description: A report on a rookie's performance.
daily.example: Rewarding the coach's trust, the rookie scored a goal.

work.title: New product launch
work.description: A company describes a new product in a press release.
work.example: In response to customer feedback, we've released a new size.

work.title: Pledge after promotion
work.description: A promoted employee speaks to their boss.
work.example: I'll do my very best to live up to the company's expectations.

etymology: 「こたえる」 was 「こたふ」 in old Japanese, meaning “to respond, to reply”. Written 「答える」, it means answering in words. Written 「応える」, it means responding to expectations or requests through action. 「〜にこたえて」 uses the latter.

similar.title: 〜に応じて
similar.explanation: Means “according to ...”; A is a changing condition (「収入に応じて」). With 「にこたえて」, A is someone's expectation or request, and you meet it.

similar.title: 〜に沿って
similar.explanation: Means “along, in line with (a policy or plan)”, focusing on not straying. 「にこたえて」 focuses on responding to and satisfying others.

similar.title: 〜に答えて
similar.explanation: 「質問に答えて」 is answering in words; 「期待に応えて」 is responding through action. Different kanji, different meaning.

meaning: “It's best to ...”, “nothing beats ...”. Usually common-sense advice.
connection: Noun／verb dictionary form／い-adj.／な-adj. + に越したことはない

senses.label: It's best to
senses.meaning: Of course ... is best; nothing is better. Usually a common-sense judgment. It often implies “it's not essential” or “if you can't, that's OK”.
senses.connection: Noun／verb dictionary form／い-adj. + に越したことはない (often followed by 「が、〜」)
examples: It never hurts to be careful.
Of course, the healthier your body, the better.
Cheaper rent is always better, but being far from the station is a problem.

senses.label: Polite form and variations
senses.meaning: The polite form is 「〜に越したことはありません」. You can also say 「〜ば、それに越したことはない」: “if ..., that would be ideal”.
senses.connection: 〜に越したことはありません; 〜ば／〜なら + それに越したことはない
examples: It's always best to prepare early.
If you can pass on the first try, that would be ideal.

notes: It expresses a general, common-sense judgment, not the speaker's personal taste.
Often followed by 「が、〜」 to make a concession: “... is best, of course, but ...”.
「越す」 means “to exceed”. Some people write 「超した」, but 「越した」 is standard.

daily.title: Taking an umbrella
daily.description: A family member tells you to take an umbrella.
daily.example: Just in case, it's better to take an umbrella.

daily.title: Talking about checkups
daily.description: Talking about health with a friend.
daily.example: It's best to get a health checkup every year.

daily.title: Choosing a computer
daily.description: Discussing with a friend at an electronics store.
daily.example: A lighter laptop is better, of course, but price matters too.

work.title: Discussing delivery with a supplier
work.description: A buyer explains priorities.
work.example: The sooner the delivery the better, of course, but please put quality first.

work.title: Advice from a senior
work.description: A senior colleague suggests a newcomer get a qualification.
work.example: It never hurts to have a qualification.

etymology: 「越す」 means “to go beyond, to exceed”. 「〜に越したことはない」 literally means “there's nothing that goes beyond ...”, i.e., “... is best”.

similar.title: 〜に限る
similar.explanation: Also means “... is best”, but it's the speaker's strong personal opinion (「夏はビールに限る」). 「に越したことはない」 is a general, common-sense judgment and softer.

similar.title: 〜ほうがいい
similar.explanation: General advice: “you'd better ...”. 「に越したことはない」 stresses “that would be ideal” and often comes with a concession.

similar.title: 〜べきだ
similar.explanation: Expresses obligation, “should ...”, and is strong. 「に越したことはない」 only says “that's best”, not that it's required.

meaning: “On the occasion of ...”, “when ...”. Used for special or important occasions. Formal and written.
connection: Noun／verb dictionary form + に際して・に際し・に際しての + noun

senses.label: On the occasion of
senses.meaning: At the time of doing something special, or just before it starts. More formal than 「〜とき」, common in speeches, notices, and official documents. 「に際し」 is more written.
senses.connection: Noun (出発・契約・入学, etc.)／verb dictionary form + に際して／に際し、／に際しては
examples: Before we depart, I'll explain some points to keep in mind.
An ID is required when signing the contract.
When I returned to my home country, I said goodbye to the people who had helped me.

senses.label: Noun modifier: ... at the time of
senses.meaning: 「に際しての + noun」 modifies a noun: “... for/at the time of ...”.
senses.connection: Noun + に際しての + noun
examples: We'd like to inform you about the admission procedures.

notes: Used for one-time, special occasions, not everyday routines. ✕「食事に際して」.
Mostly interchangeable with 「にあたって」, but 「に際して」 is more objective, focusing on “at that time”.
In formal speeches, 「〜に際しまして」 is used.

daily.title: Reading travel info
daily.description: Reading the pre-trip guide from a travel agency.
daily.example: Before traveling, please check your passport's expiration date.

daily.title: Talking about a wedding
daily.description: Telling a friend about getting married.
daily.example: When we got married, we received congratulations from many people.

work.title: Opening speech
work.description: The host speaks at the start of a conference.
work.example: To open this meeting, allow me to say a few words.

work.title: Company rules
work.description: A rule about resignation in the employee handbook.
work.example: When resigning, you must give notice at least one month in advance.

etymology: 「際」 is a Sino-Japanese word meaning “time, moment” (as in 「この際」, 「実際」). 「〜に際する」 is a formal Chinese-style expression meaning “to come to the time of ...”.

similar.title: 〜にあたって
similar.explanation: Basically the same meaning. 「にあたって」 stresses actively preparing for something important that's starting; 「に際して」 marks the time more objectively.

similar.title: 〜際（に）
similar.explanation: 「〜の際に」 works in everyday situations (「お帰りの際は」). 「に際して」 is only for special, major events and is more formal.

similar.title: 〜に先立って
similar.explanation: Clearly means “before ... (do something first)”. 「に際して」 means “at that time”.

meaning: Before something important, first doing preparation or something else. Formal and written.
connection: Noun／verb dictionary form + に先立って・に先立ち・に先立つ + noun

senses.label: Prior to
senses.meaning: Before an important event, a preliminary step happens first. The second half is what's done in advance. Common in news, notices, and ceremonies.
senses.connection: Noun (会議・発売・試合, etc.)／verb dictionary form + に先立って／に先立ち、
examples: Prior to the game, an opening ceremony was held.
Ahead of the new product's release, a press conference was held.
Before starting construction, we held a briefing for local residents.

senses.label: Preceding ...
senses.meaning: 「に先立つ + noun」 modifies a noun: “... before ...”, “preceding ...”.
senses.connection: Noun + に先立つ + noun
examples: I was invited to a preview screening before the film's release.

notes: A is a fairly formal, important event; B is preparation or an earlier activity for it.
Not used for everyday trivia. ✕「食事に先立って手を洗う」 sounds exaggerated.
On its own, 「先立つ」 can also mean “to die before (someone)”, as in 「妻に先立たれる」. That's not this grammar.

daily.title: Reading world news
daily.description: A report on a summit meeting.
daily.example: Ahead of the summit, the two countries' foreign ministers held talks.

daily.title: Watching a live game
daily.description: A commentator describes the pre-game ceremony.
daily.example: Before the start of the match, the national anthem was played.

work.title: Member pre-sale notice
work.description: A notice a company sends to its members.
work.example: Before the general release, we'll hold an advance sale for members.

work.title: Preparing for a meeting
work.description: A secretary emails the attendees.
work.example: Ahead of the meeting, I'll send you the materials.

etymology: 「先立つ」 is 「先（さき）」 + 「立つ」, originally “to stand in front, to go ahead”. It extended to “to come before in time”.

similar.title: 〜前に
similar.explanation: General “before ...”, used in both speech and writing. 「に先立って」 is formal and usually about preparing for something important.

similar.title: 〜にあたって
similar.explanation: Means “on the occasion of ...”, covering both before and during. 「に先立って」 clearly means “before”.

similar.title: 〜に先駆けて
similar.explanation: N1: “ahead of (others)”, focusing on getting ahead of others. 「に先立って」 focuses on time order.

meaning: Imagining someone's feelings or thoughts from their position: “for ..., from ...'s point of view”.
connection: Noun (person・organization) + にしたら／にすれば／にしてみれば

senses.label: From ...'s position
senses.meaning: Guessing how someone (usually another person) feels or sees things from their standpoint. Follows a noun for a person or organization. The second half is usually a guess: 「〜だろう」, 「〜かもしれない」, 「〜はずだ」.
senses.connection: Person noun + にしたら、／にすれば、
examples: For parents, their child's future is probably their biggest worry.
For the shop, rainy days must be a problem because there are fewer customers.
From his point of view, maybe it was just meant as a joke.

senses.label: Putting yourself in their shoes
senses.meaning: 「〜にしてみれば」 and 「〜にしてみたら」 stress “if you put yourself in their shoes”. Often used to show understanding of others.
senses.connection: Person noun + にしてみれば／にしてみたら
examples: From the child's point of view, cram school every day must be tough.
For the other person, I think it was awkward to be turned down so suddenly.

notes: Mostly used to guess other people's feelings. For your own view, 「私としては」 or 「私から見ると」 is more common.
Don't confuse it with 「〜にする」 for choosing: 「コーヒーにしたらどう？」 means “Why not have coffee?”.
Unlike 「にとって」, 「にしたら」 is usually followed by the other person's feelings or thoughts, not an objective evaluation.

daily.title: Getting a friend to see Mom's side
daily.description: Your friend got scolded for coming home late, and you help them see their mom's feelings.
daily.example: Put yourself in your mom's shoes. She was probably too worried to sleep.

daily.title: Noise for the neighbors
daily.description: A family member wants to play piano at night, so you remind them.
daily.example: For the neighbors, piano at night must be noisy.

daily.title: Moving with a pet
daily.description: Talking with family about how a move affects the cat.
daily.example: For a cat, moving is a big stress.

work.title: Customer experience
work.description: A store manager reminds staff in a meeting.
work.example: From the customer's point of view, long waits must be frustrating.

work.title: Being considerate of new hires
work.description: A senior colleague talks about a new employee.
work.example: For a new employee, the first month is all about learning things, so it must be hard.

etymology: Made from the conditional forms 「したら」 and 「すれば」 of 「〜にする」. 「Aにしたら」 originally means “if you set your position as A”, i.e., “if you stand in A's place”.

similar.title: 〜にとって
similar.explanation: “For ...” as an objective evaluation (「私にとって大切な人」), and can be used for yourself. 「にしたら」 focuses on guessing others' feelings and thoughts.

similar.title: 〜から見ると
similar.explanation: Judging from a viewpoint or basis, not limited to people. With 「にしたら」, A must be a person or organization.

similar.title: 〜としたら・〜とすれば
similar.explanation: A hypothetical: “if ...”. Not about someone's position.

meaning: A concession: “even if ...”, “whatever ...”. More written than 「にしても」.
connection: Noun／verb・adjective plain form + にしろ・にせよ (nouns and な-adjectives can also take 「であるにせよ」)

senses.label: Even if
senses.meaning: Even if A is accepted (as fact or hypothesis), the judgment in B doesn't change. The second half is usually the speaker's opinion, evaluation, or demand, such as 「〜べきだ」 or 「〜てはいけない」.
senses.connection: Verb・い-adj. plain form／noun + にしろ／にせよ (often with 「たとえ」 or 「どんな」)
examples: Even if you're busy, you should at least get in touch.
Whatever the reason, violence is unacceptable.
Even as a joke, you shouldn't say something like that.

senses.label: Set phrases: anyway
senses.meaning: 「いずれにせよ」, 「いずれにしろ」, 「何にせよ」, and 「どちらにしろ」 are set phrases meaning “anyway, in any case”.
senses.connection: いずれ／何／どちら + にしろ／にせよ、
examples: In any case, we have to reach a conclusion by tomorrow.
Anyway, I'm glad you're safe.

notes: 「にしろ」 and 「にせよ」 are written versions of 「にしても」. 「にせよ」 is the most written.
Don't confuse it with the imperative: 「静かにしろ！」 means “Be quiet!”, not this grammar.
There is also 「にもせよ」, as in 「一時的にもせよ」.

daily.title: Telling a friend to reply
daily.description: Your friend doesn't want to go to a party, so you remind them.
daily.example: Even if you're not going, you'd better reply.

daily.title: Reading an editorial
daily.description: A newspaper editorial gives the writer's view.
daily.example: Whatever the circumstances, rules should be followed.

daily.title: Talking about saving
daily.description: Talking about money with family.
daily.example: Even if it's just a little, it's better to save some money.

work.title: Wrapping up a meeting
work.description: The chair sums up the discussion.
work.example: In any case, let's decide on a direction by next week.

work.title: Replying to a client email
work.description: Explaining delivery progress to a client.
work.example: Even if there's a slight delay, we'll definitely meet the deadline.

etymology: 「しろ」 and 「せよ」 are both imperative forms of 「する」 (「せよ」 is the classical imperative and more written). 「Nにしろ」 literally means “let it be N”. From “granting it for now”, it became a concession: “even if ...”.

similar.title: 〜にしても
similar.explanation: Same meaning, used in both speech and writing. 「にしろ」 and 「にせよ」 are more written and stiff.

similar.title: 〜としても
similar.explanation: Focuses on “even supposing ...”, mostly hypothetical. 「にしろ」 can grant a fact or a hypothesis.

similar.title: たとえ〜ても
similar.explanation: The common spoken “even if ...”. 「にしろ」 is more written and sounds more natural after nouns.

meaning: Lists two (often opposite) cases: “whether A or B, either way ...”.
connection: Noun／verb・adjective plain form + にしろ + noun／plain form + にしろ (also 「にせよ〜にせよ」, 「にしても〜にしても」)

senses.label: Whether A or B
senses.meaning: Lists two opposite cases (such as doing or not doing): B holds either way. The second half is usually the speaker's judgment or request.
senses.connection: Verb dictionary form + にしろ + verb nai-form + にしろ
examples: Whether you go or not, please let us know early.
Whether you agree or disagree, you should state your reasons clearly.
Whether you buy it or not, it's worth having a look first.

senses.label: Listing similar things
senses.meaning: Lists two things of the same kind as examples: “whether it's A or B, it's the same”.
senses.connection: Noun + にしろ + noun + にしろ
examples: Whether it's meat or fish, choosing fresh ones is important.
Whether it's Japanese or English, daily practice is essential for learning a language.

notes: 「にせよ〜にせよ」 is the most written, 「にしても〜にしても」 is more casual, and 「にしろ〜にしろ」 is in between.
The second half is the speaker's judgment, claim, or request; it doesn't usually state a simple past fact.
When the second item uses the same verb, it can be shortened, as in 「採用するにせよしないにせよ」.

daily.title: Deciding what to eat
daily.description: Choosing a restaurant with family on the weekend.
daily.example: Whether it's Japanese or Western food, I want something tasty today.

daily.title: Advising a friend
daily.description: A friend can't decide what to do after graduation.
daily.example: Whether you study abroad or get a job, think it through before you decide.

work.title: Hiring process
work.description: An HR manager gives instructions.
work.example: Whether we hire them or not, inform the candidate of the result.

work.title: Internal notice
work.description: Explaining training attendance requirements.
work.example: Whether full-time or part-time, attending the training is mandatory.

etymology: Made by repeating the concessive 「にしろ」, 「にせよ」, or 「にしても」 twice. 「しろ」 and 「せよ」 are imperative forms of 「する」. 「Aにしろ、Bにしろ」 literally means “let it be A, let it be B”: both cases are granted, and the conclusion stays the same.

similar.title: 〜にしろ・〜にせよ
similar.explanation: Gives only one case, as a concession: “even if ...”. 「〜にしろ〜にしろ」 gives two cases: “either way ...”.

similar.title: 〜でも〜でも
similar.explanation: Casual, mainly with nouns (「肉でも魚でも」). 「にしろ〜にしろ」 is more written and can also follow verbs.

similar.title: 〜であれ〜であれ
similar.explanation: N1, written; same meaning, mainly with nouns.
